info.title: Compliance Intelligence Copilot API
info.description:
Grounded, citation-backed answers over a firm's own AML/KYC compliance documents.

**What makes the answers trustworthy**

* **Citations cannot be fabricated.** The model emits references into a set the server
  controls; the server resolves them against the passages actually retrieved and discards
  anything else. A citation can only ever point at real indexed text.
* **Refusal is enforced in code, not requested in a prompt.** When no retrieved passage
  clears the evidence floor, no answer is requested from the model at all.
* **Conflicting policy versions are surfaced, not silently resolved.**
* **Evidence strength is reported as retrieval signals plus a banded rule** — never as an
  LLM-generated confidence percentage, which would be uncalibrated.
* **Retrieval quality is measured**, not asserted: see the evaluation endpoints.

Hybrid retrieval (dense BGE embeddings + BM25, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, optional
cross-encoder reranking) over section-aware chunks carrying full document provenance.

get.description:
Always 200 while the process is serving. Deliberately checks nothing else — a liveness
probe that fails on a dependency outage causes restarts that do not fix anything.
Reports whether the service can actually answer a question right now.

Every figure here is measured from the registry, the query log, and the indices.
Unknown values are reported as zero or null rather than invented.
Secrets are never returned — only whether they are configured.

patch.description: Overrides live in process memory only and are never written to disk, so a demo can try a different model or retrieval configuration without altering the deployment's configuration. Enabling reranking loads the cross-encoder on first use.

post.description: Returns a grounded answer with citations resolved against the retrieved passages, an evidence band derived from retrieval signals, and any version conflicts found. A superset of the v1 CLI response shape.

Server-sent events in a fixed order: `conversation` → `meta` → `retrieval` → `token`* → `citations` → `evidence` → (`conflicts`) → `done`. An `error` event replaces whatever would have followed. Citation markers emitted by the model are resolved server-side against the retrieved set, so the `citations` event can only ever contain real passages.

post.summary: Upload and index one or more documents
post.description: Accepts .md, .txt, .pdf and .docx. Files are validated by extension **and** magic bytes, size-capped, stored content-addressed, then extracted, cleaned, chunked with full heading provenance, scanned for injection patterns, embedded, and indexed. Identical content is deduplicated rather than indexed twice.

patch.summary: Activate/deactivate a document or correct its metadata
patch.description: Deactivating excludes a document from retrieval while keeping it inspectable — the honest way to supersede a policy without destroying the audit trail that references it. Metadata corrections apply to the registry; re-index to refresh chunk copies.

delete.summary: Delete a document and remove its chunks from both indices

parameters.name: purge_original

schema.description: Also delete the stored original file.
schema.title: Purge Original

parameters.description: Also delete the stored original file.

post.summary: Re-run the ingestion pipeline for a document
post.description: Needed after a chunking or embedding change. Idempotent: the same document produces the same chunk identities.

get.summary: Full transcript with citations and evidence per message

delete.description: Removes the UI transcript only. The audit log deliberately retains every query and the context it was answered from — an audit trail a user can erase is not an audit trail.

post.description: `retrieval_only` computes Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR, nDCG@5 and section accuracy by exact arithmetic with no LLM involved — deterministic and CI-safe. `full` adds generation metrics (citation precision/recall, keyword and numeric compliance, refusal accuracy) and, with `judge=true`, LLM-judged faithfulness and relevance which are reported as indicative rather than ground truth.

ActivityEntry.title: ActivityEntry
ActivityEntry.description: Analytics only — a question hash, never the question text (see README §16).

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Omit to start a new conversation.

use_history.title: Use History
use_history.description: Use conversation history to rewrite follow-up questions.

example.question: What are the KYC requirements for high-risk customers?

ChatResponse.title: ChatResponse
ChatResponse.description: A superset of the v1 CLI response: the original seven fields are unchanged.

Citation.title: Citation
Citation.description:
What the UI renders and what an auditor verifies.

`document` and `chunk` are the original (v1) field names and are retained verbatim so
the CLI's documented JSON contract still holds; everything else is additive.

injection_flags.title: Injection Flags
injection_flags.description: Spans that look like prompt injection. Flagged for human review; answers are protected structurally regardless (see README §17).

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Every non-2xx response in this API has this shape.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: retrieval_only is deterministic and needs no LLM; full adds generation.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Derived from retrieval signals, not a calibrated probability. Always verify the cited passages.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description:
Retrieval-derived evidence strength. Explicitly NOT a confidence probability —
see README DR-11.

include_inactive.title: Include Inactive
include_inactive.description: Include deactivated/superseded documents. Off by default so a superseded policy is never returned as a current rule.

SettingsPatchRequest.title: SettingsPatchRequest
SettingsPatchRequest.description: Session-scoped overrides — never written to disk.

SettingsResponse.title: SettingsResponse
SettingsResponse.description: Secrets are never returned — only whether they are configured.

StageTimings.title: StageTimings
StageTimings.description:
Per-stage latency, surfaced in the response as well as the logs so a slow answer is
attributable without reading a log file.

StatsResponse.title: StatsResponse
StatsResponse.description:
Dashboard aggregates.

Fully typed rather than a bare dict so the generated frontend types are usable: an
untyped `dict[str, Any]` here becomes `Record<string, unknown>` in TypeScript, which
pushes every field access back to runtime. Typing it means a renamed field breaks the
build instead of the dashboard.

TokenUsage.title: TokenUsage
TokenUsage.description:
Null rather than estimated when the provider does not report usage (Ollama).
A guessed token count in a cost dashboard is worse than no token count.

UploadFailure.title: UploadFailure
UploadFailure.description:
A per-file rejection. Typed rather than a free-form dict so the frontend can render
it without casting — the same reason StatsResponse is typed.

duplicate_of.title: Duplicate Of
duplicate_of.description: Set when identical content was already indexed; no duplicate was created.
